issues.issue: The precedence rule says the Agreement prevails over an inconsistent Confirmation 'unless each party has executed such Confirmation', leaving it unclear which document governs when only one party signs or when the Confirmation is made through a comparison system under 2.1(b).

Section 2.1 makes the Agreement prevail over inconsistent Confirmations, while Schedule B section 2 makes the Schedule prevail over the Agreement, leaving a three-document hierarchy that is nowhere fully ordered.
The sentence is broken mid-clause ('regarding when a Loan unless otherwise agreed'), so the condition it purports to override cannot be identified from the words used.

Section 2.2 says no Loan occurs until both Loaned Securities and Collateral have been transferred, while Section 4.1 expressly contemplates Collateral being transferred after the securities (up to Close of Business that day) and Section 4.4 addresses one-sided transfers.

The recharacterisation trigger, 'if any Loan is deemed to be a loan of money', does not say by whom or on what standard the deeming occurs, so the condition on which the security interest arises is undefined.
The required amount is the 'Margin Percentage' of Market Value, and that percentage is defined twice with different content in Section 25.37 and Schedule B section 6.

'Lender may use or invest the Collateral, if such consists of cash, at its own risk' is open to two readings: that the Lender bears investment losses on cash collateral, or merely that it acts without the Borrower's warranty while the loss allocation lies elsewhere. The same sentence's segregation duty ('unless Lender is a Broker-Dealer') sits awkwardly with a permission to invest.
'Absolute right to the return' is not tied to any procedure or time limit, and it is unclear how it interacts with the Section 13 remedies for the same failure to transfer.
The proviso setting out what substituted Collateral must consist of breaks off after '(a) consist only of cash,', so the conditions on substitution cannot be applied as written.

The carve-out reads 'Except as set forth in Sections 3.1 and 8.2', but Section 3.1 concerns Lender's transfer of securities and contains no exception to Borrower's incidents of ownership; the intended reference is evidently Section 8.1.
The final obligation is cut off ('Borrower shall forthwith transfer the ...'), so what must be transferred on a terminated Loan is not stated.

The conditional structure is broken: clause (a) reads 'transfer of cash cash or other property by Lender would give rise to a Margin Deficit' and the counterpart limb (Borrower/Margin Excess) is missing, so the trigger for crediting instead of transferring cannot be applied.

Section 9.1 fixes a flat 100% collateral level for Customer loans, while Sections 9.2/25.37 and Schedule B section 6 set the requirement by reference to a 'Margin Percentage' that may be higher, and the two mark-to-market regimes are not expressly reconciled.
The demand right runs on the 'Margin Percentage', which Section 25.37 and Schedule B section 6 define differently, so the level triggering a Margin Deficit depends on which definition controls.

The representation is qualified by compliance with 'Section 11.1(b)', which requires execution of 'Annex I', but the annex made applicable by Schedule B section 1 is Annex I-A, so the condition points to a document not incorporated by that name.
The waiver refers to 'the representation or warranty in subsection (6)', a mis-citation of subsection (a), so the representation being disapplied is identified only by inference.

Section 11.1(b) requires execution of and compliance with 'Annex I', but Schedule B section 1 makes 'Annex I-A (Agency Annex)' the applicable annex, leaving the agency election tied to a differently named document.

The remedy turns on purchasing replacement securities and selling Collateral 'in a commercially reasonable manner', an unmeasured standard that also governs the damages computation against the Borrower.

Borrower's remedy likewise depends on the undefined 'commercially reasonable manner' standard, and on a deemed-price election 'in its sole discretion' from 'a generally recognized source', with no criterion for choosing that source.

Where no generally recognised price source exists the non-defaulting party may fix the source 'in its sole discretion', with no standard limiting that choice even though it sets the measure of damages.

The clause defines 'securities' to include 'security entitlements' 'as used herein (except in this Section 15)', an exclusion that is hard to square with the same Section's rules on transferring 'financial assets' and obtaining 'control'.
